purpose: Teach: 前列/鮓/峪/壱/魏/起る/不確か/組成

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、講演の前列、つまり前列席の聴衆動向の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your paper was on audience behavior patterns in lecture front rows, wasn't it?
lines.style: Warm, genuinely curious. Steady eye contact. Gentle confirmation rather than interrogation—she already knows the answer and is giving him space to own it.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、寿司、つまり鮓、つまり古い表記の鮓の食文化研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, my paper examined the food culture of sushi—the older character form—through a linguistic and historical lens.
lines.style: Slightly hesitant, gathering thoughts mid-sentence. Earnest but a touch self-conscious about the specificity. Clear enunciation on the key terms, like he's practiced this explanation.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、山の峪、つまり峪の地形研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your research looked at the topography of mountain valleys and their geological formations, right?
lines.style: Thoughtful pause before speaking. Gentle, almost musing tone—she's drawing out understanding as much as confirming. Slight tilt of the head.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、旧字「壱」、つまり一の用法研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I wrote about the usage patterns of the older character form for 'one'—壱 versus the modern form—and how that evolved in written Japanese.
lines.style: Measured, slightly defensive in its precision. He's aware there's a mismatch and he's trying to own it clearly. No apology in the tone, just straightforward commitment to accuracy.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、三国時代の魏王朝の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, didn't your paper examine the Wei Dynasty during the Three Kingdoms period?
lines.style: Gentle curiosity with a knowing undertone. She's testing something—not harshly, but with the warmth of someone who notices patterns. Slight rise at the end, inviting him to reflect.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、事件が起る、つまり「起る」の用法の言語学研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Actually, I focused on the linguistic usage of an older verb form—'okoru'—and how it was used differently across historical texts and modern writing.
lines.style: Quieter but steady. He's not defensive, just clarifying. Slight emphasis on the linguistic framing to anchor his actual research. Almost apologetic in rhythm but not in content.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、感染症の不確かさを巡る疫学研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your epidemiological work centered on uncertainty in infectious disease prediction, didn't it?
lines.style: Reflective, almost gently testing. The rhythm suggests she's watching how he responds—patient, interested, but with a subtle hint of gentle challenge underneath.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、岩石の組成分析の地質学研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: No, I wrote a geological study analyzing the mineral composition and structure of rock formations.
lines.style: Calm but direct. The correction is matter-of-fact, not irritated. Closes with finality—he's done explaining, settled into what he actually knows. Slight exhale of relief at clarity.
